gaps.sentence: At midnight, the protesters ___ outside the parliament, refusing to move.
gaps.hint: at midnight, in progress at that point
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific past moment takes the past continuous: were standing.

gaps.sentence: Look at Sam — he ___ at that stranger again.
gaps.hint: look draws attention to this moment
gaps.explanation: 'Look' draws attention to something happening now, so the present continuous is used: is staring.

gaps.sentence: We ___ our cousins in Melbourne next month — the flights are booked.
gaps.hint: a booked arrangement for next month
gaps.explanation: A fixed personal arrangement takes the present continuous: are visiting.

gaps.sentence: By Friday, the climbers ___ on the north face for six days without a break.
gaps.hint: duration measured to a future point
gaps.explanation: 'By Friday + for six days' calls for the future perfect: will have been.

gaps.sentence: Our team ___ the championship twice in the last five years.
gaps.hint: in the last five years up to now
gaps.explanation: 'In the last five years' is a period up to the present, so the present perfect fits: has won.

gaps.sentence: Hush! The director ___ about the budget at the moment.
gaps.hint: at the moment shows active thinking process
gaps.explanation: Here 'think' describes a mental process in progress, not an opinion, so the continuous is used: is thinking.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her keys again — this is the third time this month!
gaps.hint: third time this month connects to now
gaps.explanation: 'This is the third time' links a recent event to now, so the present perfect is required: has lost.

gaps.sentence: The soup ___ delicious, but I think it needs a little more salt.
gaps.hint: taste describing a quality is stative
gaps.explanation: When 'taste' describes a quality of something, it is a state verb: tastes.
